summary: The PR removes a guard check (`if (!user.address)`) in `getUserCity`, introducing a regression where passing a user object without an `address` property (or with `address` set to `null`/`undefined`) throws a runtime `TypeError` instead of safely returning `null`.

findings.title: TypeError thrown when user object lacks address property
findings.description: Removing the check for `!user.address` causes `getUserCity` to attempt direct property access `user.address.city`. When `user.address` is `undefined` or `null`, Node.js throws a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city')`. This breaks callers expecting `null` when an address is not present.
findings.verificationHypothesis: Calling `getUserCity({ name: 'Alice' })` or `getUserCity({ address: null })` will throw a `TypeError` instead of returning `null`.

suggestedReproduction.preconditions: src/users.js is loaded in a Node.js environment.
suggestedReproduction.expectedBehavior: getUserCity returns null when user.address is missing.
suggestedReproduction.suspiciousBehavior: getUserCity throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city').
